newsitem.title: UK: PolyGram not expecting film profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: PolyGram not expecting film profit in 1997.

text.p: PolyGram president and CEO Alain Levy said on Wednesday that the company was not expecting its film division to make a profit this year.
PolyGram Filmed Entertainment (PFE), set up five years ago, crept into profit in the second half of 1996 but Levy said this would not be repeated this year.

He said PFE's plans to establish its own major distribution business in the U.S. in the last quarter of 1997 and a move to making bigger budget movies would make this a "transitional year" for the division.
Levy said that PFE had operating profit of some two million guilders in the second half of 1996. Its full-year losses fell to 35 million guilders from 68 million guilders in 1995.

Looking at the company as a whole, Levy said that the high levels of sterling and the dollar should have a positive impact on its 1997 earnings if maintained. But he joked that it was even harder to forecast interest rates than to pick hit albums.
PolyGram confirmed that it was switching to quarterly reporting, its first quarter 1997 figures to be released on April 22.
